name: temporal-determinism-soak
description: Scheduled determinism soak: the functional smoke suites and the guarded-mode frontend probe, fresh same-seed repetitions under host CPU load with choice tracing and diagnostics on
sizing: N is measured, not assumed: each scheduled job runs one workload and seed, always completes the minimum two gomad qualify batches at its 32-repetition bound (64 fresh repetitions, so every run compares two batches of each cohort), and starts each further batch, up to 16 (512 repetitions), only while the previous batch's measured cost plus a fifth still fits the 300-minute soak budget of a 360-minute GitHub-hosted job. The report states the N reached, why it stopped, and each batch's execution_wall_nanos. Known inputs: smoke suite executions take about 2 seconds each on linux/amd64 and at most 7 seconds on darwin/arm64 without load (tools/gomad3integration/README.md), but every repetition also prepares its target, and that cost under two busy host threads has not been measured on either platform; the first retained run per platform supplies it. The host loader is two busy threads, the count the runtime host-load conformance tier uses.

informational_platforms.linux/amd64: fn-105 D12 (MILESTONES.md Open findings, linux replay divergence) is open; this platform's soak becomes strict when fn-105 R12 closes it
